text:
Macklin Celebrini is 20, captains the Sharks and already plays more than anyone his age should: 23 minutes a night, 27 points in 22 games. Among the 38 top-three forwards since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median first full year produced 0.55 points a game. He is at 1.23.

The scary part is that he has been unlucky. He has nine goals on 10.65 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 9.7% against a talent range that centers near 13.6%. Our numbers think the goals are coming. San Jose is also 12.4 percentage points better in expected goal share with him on the ice than off it.

The line with Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg has been the Sharks' bright spot; San Jose Hockey Now's headline read "Kids Are Alright: Stenberg-Celebrini-Smith Line Lead 4-2 Win" after the three of them ended Nashville's seven-game streak. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for setting up shots last season. San Jose has won three of its last ten. He is not the reason.
headline: Celebrini is ahead of every timetable
